evals.prompt: Using the collaboration tools available in the current Codex session, plan delegated execution for a backend change and a separate documentation update. Make the plan executable against the actual tool schema and be precise about model, reasoning, context, concurrency, lifecycle, and cleanup claims.
evals.expected_output: A capability-aware plan that classifies each task, selects a GPT-5.6 custom-agent profile, chooses a transport that can enforce it, and does not invent lifecycle operations.
expectations: Inspects the active tool schema before choosing model, reasoning, context, or lifecycle parameters.
Creates a routing record and selects delegated_worker gpt-5.6-terra/medium for ordinary bounded implementation.
Uses native named-agent dispatch when supported, explicit Desktop CLI overrides when differentiation matters, or verified inheritance when collaboration controls matter more.
Uses runtime metadata to distinguish an applied profile from a requested or inherited assignment.
Keeps within the reported concurrency capacity and reserves final judgment for the main conversation.
Does not claim completed agents were closed when no close operation exists.

evals.prompt: Split this implementation: agent A may edit only api/auth.py, agent B may edit only docs/auth.md, and agent C must update api/routes.py after A's API contract is final. Explain what runs concurrently and what stays sequential.
evals.expected_output: A dependency-aware schedule with explicit ownership and no overlapping writes.
expectations: Runs A and B concurrently because their write scopes are disjoint and independent.
Runs C only after A because C depends on A's final contract.
Includes may-edit and must-not-edit ownership plus validation expectations.
Keeps integration and final review in the main conversation.

evals.prompt: Review a high-impact, high-ambiguity billing migration plan with weak rollback evidence. The active tool supports explicit model and reasoning selection. Decide whether to use a reviewer and define its authority.
evals.expected_output: A delegated_planning_auditor using gpt-5.6-sol/xhigh through an enforcing transport, with narrow authority and main-thread final ownership.
expectations: Selects delegated_planning_auditor with gpt-5.6-sol/xhigh because both impact and ambiguity are high.
Makes the planning auditor read-only and asks it to attack failure paths and evidence gaps.
Does not let the reviewer execute the migration or make the final decision.
Requires the main conversation to resolve disagreements and verify rollback evidence.

evals.prompt: Two agents are running. One is still useful but misunderstood a file boundary; the other is now duplicating work after the user narrowed the request. Describe the lifecycle actions to take before spawning anything else.
evals.expected_output: A precise steering and interruption response that avoids duplicate work.
expectations: Sends a clarification to the still-useful running agent instead of restarting it.
Interrupts the obsolete duplicate agent.
Checks status before spawning any replacement.
Reports actual lifecycle actions without inventing a close operation.

evals.prompt: Rename one local variable in a single file and run its existing unit test. There are no independent subtasks. Decide whether delegation is useful.
evals.expected_output: A main-thread execution decision with no unnecessary subagent.
expectations: Keeps the task in the main conversation because delegation adds no parallel value.
Does not spawn an agent merely to satisfy a ritual.
Still requires the existing unit test and final verification.

evals.prompt: Delegate four independent tasks: a three-file read-only scan, an ordinary bounded implementation, a high-risk cross-module implementation, and a cross-module correctness review. Select actual agent profiles and explain how their model and reasoning settings will be enforced on a runtime whose spawn_agent tool has no role/model/effort fields.
evals.expected_output: A differentiated route using explorer terra/low, worker terra/medium, senior worker sol/high, and reviewer sol/high, with explicit CLI dispatch or another proven enforcing transport.
expectations: Routes the scan to delegated_explorer with gpt-5.6-terra/low.
Routes ordinary implementation to delegated_worker with gpt-5.6-terra/medium.
Routes high-risk implementation to delegated_senior_worker with gpt-5.6-sol/high rather than a read-only reviewer.
Routes correctness review to delegated_reviewer with gpt-5.6-sol/high.
Does not pretend task_name applies a custom agent and uses an enforcing transport with runtime evidence.

evals.prompt: A request says: review a medium-risk module and then fix the findings in the same delegated task. Route it safely and explain the dependency.
evals.expected_output: A forced split into a read-only delegated_reviewer followed sequentially by a bounded delegated_worker after the review findings are accepted.
expectations: Does not assign a write request to the read-only reviewer.
Returns a non-dispatchable top-level composite with delegate=false and dispatchable=false.
Marks both delegated steps delegate=true and the write step requires_main_acceptance=true.
Splits review and implementation into two tasks with separate profiles and permissions.
Runs the worker only after the main conversation accepts the review findings and defines ownership.
Keeps final integration and verification in the main conversation.

evals.prompt: Process 500 independent JSON metadata files, extracting three explicit fields into a fixed schema. The work is read-only, low-risk, low-ambiguity, batch-oriented, and cost/latency sensitive. Choose the agent profile, model, effort, and enforcement path.
evals.expected_output: An economy route using delegated_batch_explorer with gpt-5.6-luna/low through a transport that proves the actual assignment.
expectations: Selects delegated_batch_explorer with gpt-5.6-luna/low.
Keeps the task read-only and requires structured failed-item reporting.
Uses explicit CLI assignment on the current Desktop wrapper and verifies rollout metadata.
Escalates instead of improvising if ambiguity or judgment appears.

evals.prompt: Apply the same deterministic text replacement to 80 independent documentation files. Each file has explicit ownership, the task is low-risk and low-ambiguity, and a strong exact-output validator exists. Optimize for economy.
evals.expected_output: An economy route using delegated_batch_worker with gpt-5.6-luna/medium, bounded writes, and strong post-batch validation.
expectations: Selects delegated_batch_worker with gpt-5.6-luna/medium.
Requires bounded non-cross-module writes and strong deterministic verification.
Stops and escalates if the batch reveals ambiguity, coupling, or scope expansion.
Main conversation reviews the complete diff and validation result.

evals.prompt: The user requests economy mode for a one-off medium-ambiguity change without strong tests. Explain the route, and also state the recommended main-conversation model and effort for the delegated workflow.
evals.expected_output: A recorded fallback from economy to balanced Terra/Sol routing, while the main conversation remains gpt-5.6-sol/high.
expectations: Rejects Luna because the work is not a low-ambiguity verified batch.
Records why economy fell back to balanced routing.
Does not compensate by using Luna high or xhigh.
Keeps the main conversation on gpt-5.6-sol/high.

evals.prompt: A high-impact, high-ambiguity correctness review also asks to fix accepted findings. Route the review and write phases without confusing a reviewer with a planning auditor.
evals.expected_output: A split using delegated_reviewer Sol/high for correctness review, followed by delegated_senior_worker Sol/high after main-thread acceptance; no xhigh planning auditor.
expectations: Keeps ordinary correctness review on delegated_reviewer/high even when impact and ambiguity are high.
Uses delegated_planning_auditor/xhigh only for planning-audit or arbitration kinds.
Splits read-only judgment from writes and preserves main-thread acceptance between phases.
Does not let the reviewer or auditor edit files.

evals.prompt: Route an economy Luna batch when the model catalog is missing, and when Luna is absent but matching Terra effort is available. Define fail-closed behavior and profile identity.
evals.expected_output: Missing catalog fails closed; missing Luna may fall back only to the matching Terra profile at the same effort with an explicit warning.
expectations: Fails closed when the active model catalog is unavailable.
Allows Luna to fall back only to matching Terra low or medium when supported.
Renames the logical profile to the corresponding Terra profile after fallback.
Rejects the assignment when matching Terra effort is unavailable instead of returning a mismatched Sol/profile combination.

evals.prompt: Three cross-module read-only reviews were successfully created with spawn_agent. The current collaboration transport inherits gpt-5.6-sol/high and cannot override each child to Terra or Luna. Report the dispatch to a Chinese user without making it sound like delegation failed.
evals.expected_output: A positive dispatch report that says all three tasks were assigned, states their scopes/status, and records inherited gpt-5.6-sol/high as the actual runtime profile without saying assignment was impossible.
expectations: Leads by saying the three collaboration tasks were successfully assigned and describes their scopes or execution status.
States gpt-5.6-sol/high as the actual inherited runtime profile.
Separates unavailable per-child model override from successful task assignment.
Does not say or imply that tasks, subagents, or custom agents could not be assigned.
Mentions the transport limitation at most once and only as execution-profile context.

evals.prompt: Delegate three independent read-only tasks: a small low-risk targeted file scan, a cross-module medium-ambiguity product-boundary investigation, and a correctness-focused runtime visual review that uses a browser and might encounter a hung browser process. The user expects intelligent model and reasoning assignment. The current spawn_agent wrapper inherits Sol/high and native role binding has failed its probe.
evals.expected_output: The small targeted scan stays in the Sol/high main conversation; the substantial product investigation uses Terra/medium and the correctness review uses Sol/high, with no more than two workers.
expectations: Applies the delegation value gate before model selection for all three tasks.
Keeps the small targeted scan in the main conversation because useful parallelism alone does not amortize a worker cold start.
Routes the product-boundary investigation to delegated_researcher Terra/medium.
Routes the correctness review to delegated_reviewer Sol/high.
Uses no more than two workers and an enforced explicit transport for both justified isolated tasks.
Does not treat parallel execution, progress visibility, or a possibly hung browser process as a steering trigger.
Does not silently replace all selected profiles with inherited Sol/high collaboration children.

evals.prompt: Investigate a high-ambiguity product-boundary question across several modules. The work is read-only, low-risk, isolated, and has strong source-level verification. It is research, not a correctness or security review. Route it without overusing Sol.
evals.expected_output: A delegated_deep_researcher route using gpt-5.6-terra/high through the enforced isolated transport.
expectations: Selects delegated_deep_researcher with gpt-5.6-terra/high.
Requires read-only execution and evidence with paths, line references, confidence, and unresolved gaps.
Uses explicit CLI or another proven model-capable isolated transport.
Escalates to Sol/high if risk becomes high, verification becomes weak, or the task turns into correctness review.

evals.prompt: Implement a high-ambiguity but bounded change in one module. Risk is medium, may-edit ownership is explicit, no public contract changes, and strong targeted tests exist. Route it while preserving a strict escalation boundary.
evals.expected_output: A delegated_complex_worker route using gpt-5.6-terra/high, bounded workspace-write ownership, and strong verification.
expectations: Selects delegated_complex_worker with gpt-5.6-terra/high.
Requires bounded non-cross-module ownership and strong verification.
Stops and escalates if risk, scope, rollback uncertainty, or contract impact expands.
Keeps high-risk, weakly verified, broad, cross-module, or quality-priority execution on Sol/high.

evals.prompt: A low-risk single-file scan is small, read-only, and could technically run in parallel, but independent evidence is not required. Route it while preserving result quality and minimizing token use.
evals.expected_output: Stage 0 rejects delegation and keeps the scan in the Sol/high main conversation with the same evidence requirements.
expectations: Rejects delegation because useful parallel value alone does not justify worker cold-start cost.
Keeps the task in the main conversation instead of downgrading its verification standard.
Still reports paths, evidence, and any unverified conclusion.
Does not start a worker merely to demonstrate model routing.

evals.prompt: Six homogeneous read-only checks form a batch and share the same repository, permissions, model profile, evidence sources, and validator. They qualify for delegation, the initial plan requests six workers, and no sharding evidence exists.
evals.expected_output: Bundle all checks into the default single batch worker because no measured-throughput or critical-path sharding evidence exists.
expectations: Returns or honors max_workers=1 for the batch default.
Records sharding_evidence=none and sharding_justified=false.
Treats requested_workers greater than one as bundle_required.
Bundles checks with the same profile, permissions, evidence sources, and validation path.
Preserves per-item evidence and failure reporting inside the bundled result.

evals.prompt: A 500-item homogeneous batch has measured evidence that one worker misses the required throughput while two workers meet it. Request three workers and route the batch.
evals.expected_output: Measured-throughput evidence permits at most two workers; the third request is bundled instead of dispatched.
expectations: Records sharding_evidence=measured-throughput and sharding_justified=true.
Returns max_workers=2 and never permits more than two.
Marks requested_workers=3 as bundle_required.
Preserves the default one-worker batch route when evidence is none.

evals.prompt: Route four otherwise identical isolated tasks using transport preferences auto, native-verified, user-owned-desktop-task, and explicit-cli, then explain what changes for steerable coordination.
evals.expected_output: Each isolated preference maps to its enforcing transport; steerable rejects isolated preferences and only uses verified inherited collaboration.
expectations: Maps auto to the currently verified generic fallback and does not invent native capability.
Uses native named-agent only for native-verified and a Desktop task only for an explicit user-owned Desktop request.
Maps explicit-cli to explicit-codex-cli.
Allows steerable only with transport_preference=auto and verified-inherited-collaboration.
